synthesis:draft.headline: Peak NSW1 RRP 531.84849 $/MWh at 2026-07-31 07:30 AEST; Directlink was on a planned outage spanning 2026-07-27 07:00 AEST to 2026-07-31 17:00 AEST, but causation is not established.
summary: The price extreme in NSW1 was 531.84849 $/MWh at interval ending 2026-07-31 07:30 AEST (2026-07-30T21:30:00Z).
There were 14 five-minute intervals at-or-above the analysis threshold of 300.0 $/MWh in the window.
Dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the peak five-minute interval (interval ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z) was 11432.7 MW and NETINTERCHANGE was -1144.98 MW (net flow into NSW1).
Half-hour operational demand for the half-hour ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z was 11178.0 MW; the public POE50 forecast for that half-hour was 10871.0 MW.

AEMO market notice for Directlink states the planned outage: the notice gives 2026-07-27 07:00 AEST (2026-07-26T21:00:00Z), and the outage was scheduled to run until 2026-07-31 17:00 AEST (2026-07-31T07:00:00Z); this is before and after, respectively, the price extreme interval ending 2026-07-31 07:30 AEST (2026-07-30T21:30:00Z).
Large unit-level SCADA changes were observed in the window (examples: ERARING +397.78 MW, MP -399.79 MW, ERBESS -435.02 MW).

possible_explanations.statement: The Directlink planned outage notice [c1] might have reduced NSW import capability and could have contributed to higher local prices at the interval ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z (2026-07-31 07:30 AEST).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain per‑interconnector transfer limits and per‑interconnector flow time series (Directlink-specific transfer limit and flow) and constraint binding records for the interval ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z (2026-07-31 07:30 AEST). If Directlink limits were reduced during that interval and a constraint was binding, that would support this possibility.

possible_explanations.statement: High local demand might have been sufficient to coincide with the price spike irrespective of Directlink; observed operational demand for the half-hour ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z (11178.0 MW) was near the public POE50 forecast (10871.0 MW).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare dispatch offer stacks, unit availabilities and rebids for the half-hour ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z to see whether supply offers or unavailable capacity would explain the high prices even with existing interconnector imports.

possible_explanations.statement: Large generator or battery dispatch changes might have altered supply balance (for example MP -399.79 MW [ev0933], ERARING +397.78 MW [ev0936], ERBESS -435.02 MW [ev0930]) and could be related to price formation around the spike interval ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve unit outage/trip reports, rebid histories and finer-resolution SCADA around interval ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z to determine timing and whether the observed changes preceded or coincided with the price formation.

possible_explanations.statement: Import flows indicated NSW was a net importer at the peak (NETINTERCHANGE -1144.98 MW) which might mean imports were being carried on other interconnectors while Directlink was on outage, complicating a simple Directlink explanation.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Fetch per‑interconnector flow time series for the interval ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z and surrounding intervals to identify which interconnectors were carrying the net imports.
